Interactive D3 waterfall chart

pv_waterfall.Rd

Signed contributions building left to right from a start value: each bar floats where the running total left off, gains in the palette's first blue, losses in the theme's diverging red pole, and thin connectors carry the level across the gaps. A distinct grey-inked total bar closes the sequence (and, when start is not zero, an equally distinct start bar opens it). Value labels ride the bars where they fit; the tooltip always has the exact contribution and the running total after it.

Usage

pv_waterfall(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  start = 0,
  total = TRUE,
  value_labels = "auto",
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 500,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per contribution, in the order the bars should build — more than one row per category is an error; aggregate it first. Rows with a missing category or value are dropped with a warning; infinite values are an error, because a bar cannot float to infinity.

x

Name of the category column naming each contribution.

y

Name of the signed numeric contribution column.

start

The value the running total starts from (default 0). A non-zero start is drawn as its own "Start" bar in the total ink, so the floating bars never hang from an invisible ledge.

total

Close the sequence with a bar for the final running total? TRUE (default) labels it "Total"; a single string uses that as the label instead; FALSE ends on the last contribution.

value_labels

Print each bar's value on the chart — signed for the contributions, plain for the start and total bars. TRUE always, FALSE never; "auto" (default) shows them when at most 12 bars leave each one wide enough to carry a number.

xlab, ylab

Axis titles. NULL (default) uses the column names; NA or "" suppresses the title entirely; any other string replaces it.

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Entrance transition length in ms.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Examples

lu <- pv_city_population[pv_city_population$city == "Luzern", ]
lu <- lu[order(lu$year), ]
steps <- data.frame(
  period = paste(head(lu$year, -1), lu$year[-1], sep = "\u2013"),
  change = diff(lu$population))
pv_waterfall(steps, x = "period", y = "change",
             start = lu$population[1],
             title = "How Lucerne's population moved")
